We keep track of the start offset of the block group with the lowest start
offset at fs_info->first_logical_byte. This requires explicitly updating
that field every time we add
column2: delete or lookup a block group to/from the

column1: red black tree at fs_info->block_group_cache_tree.
Since the block group with the lowest start address happens to always be
the one that is the leftmost node of the tree
column2: we can use a red black tree

column1: that caches the left most node. Then when we need the start address of
that block group
column2: we can just quickly get the leftmost node in the tree

column1: and extract the start offset of that node's block group. This avoids the
need to explicitly keep track of that address in the dedicated member
fs_info->first_logical_byte
column2: and it also allows the next patch in the

column1: series to switch the lock that protects the red black tree from a spin
lock to a read/write lock - without this change it would be tricky
because block group searches also update fs_info->first_logical_byte.
